_comment: Declarative/tunable parts of each detection rule — keyword lists, required patterns, which artifact each rule reads, which device_types it applies to. The structural evaluation logic itself lives in engine.py as a small named function per rule (these checks are inherently block/baseline-structured, not flat field comparisons — see engine.py's module docstring). Enable/disable per rule via config.json's detection_rules block, not here. insecure-mgmt-plane/weak-snmp-community/missing-aaa deliberately exclude juniper_junos and vyos — those patterns match Cisco/Arista IOS-style config syntax specifically (transport input, snmp-server community, aaa authentication login), none of which exist in Junos/VyOS's set-style config syntax. unauthorized-local-accounts DOES cover vyos/juniper_junos too — engine.py dispatches to a vendor-specific extractor per device_type (Cisco's 'username <name>' lines vs. VyOS/Junos's 'set system login user <name>' lines), so this one rule is genuinely correct across both syntax families rather than excluded.

rules._note: arista_eos excluded — EOS has no EEM-equivalent event/action engine (real platform limitation, confirmed via collectors/arista_eos.py). baseline_required: presence-type rule, see engine.py module docstring.
Cisco/Arista-family only — Junos/VyOS use image-based boot systems, not a 'boot system <path>' config line.

Best-effort version-identifier check, not cryptographic hash verification — see knowledge_base.py's entry and engine.py's _eval_image_hash_mismatch(). Pure-diff rule: no finding at all when known_good_image_hashes is unpopulated.
Cisco/Arista-family only — 'no logging'/'logging buffered <n>' is IOS-style config syntax.
Cisco/Arista-family only — 'logging host'/'logging server' is IOS-style config syntax. Allowlist-membership rule: no finding when expected_syslog_servers is unpopulated (nothing to compare against).
vyos excluded — no native TACACS+/RADIUS command-accounting subsystem comparable to Cisco's, confirmed real platform limitation from the original design brief.
vyos excluded — no native SPAN/port-mirroring feature comparable to switch platforms (real platform limitation, confirmed via collectors/vyos.py).
Cisco/Arista-family only — 'interface Tunnel' is IOS-style config syntax.

Cisco/Arista-family only — the 'permit ip any any' keyword pattern doesn't appear in Junos/VyOS's firewall-filter syntax, so applies_to is scoped to where this check can actually match something (not excluded for platform-limitation reasons like the others above — just a regex-coverage gap).

vyos excluded — the real running-vs-saved diff command is 'compare saved', which only works inside configuration mode. This collector deliberately never enters configuration mode (read-only, operational-mode-only by design), so there's no valid read-only equivalent on VyOS.
Applies to all vendors — engine.py's section-extraction regex covers both Cisco-style (aaa/access-list/ip route) and Junos/VyOS-style (set system login/set protocols) syntax in the same pass.

Scoped to cisco_ios/cisco_ios_xe (show ip nat translations) and vyos (show conntrack table ipv4) — the only device types with a confirmed-real, read-only session/NAT table this collector can query. cisco_nxos/arista_eos/juniper_junos are typically not doing NAT/stateful conntrack in this collector's supported roles, and no verified read-only equivalent was found for them. Unlike device-outbound-c2 (the device's OWN sockets), this rule inspects the device's forwarded/transit traffic — e.g. a workstation behind the router reaching a known-bad IP — checked against config.json's threat_intel.malicious_ip_sources blocklist rather than an 'expected' baseline.
